newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian stocks end mixed in active trade.
newsitem.headline: Colombian stocks end mixed in active trade.

text.p: Colombian stocks ended mixed after a day of active trading. Medellin's IBOMED general price index gained 0.57 percent to end at 17,290.91 on trading volume of nearly 3 billion pesos. Bogota's IBB slipped 0.43 percent, closing at 1,120.49 on volume of about 1.5 billion.

Movers were led by Banco de Colombia and cement maker Cementos Argos. Banco de Colombia fell under strong selling pressure early in the session, after the bank, the country's second largest in assets, announced it had given up on plans to form a strategic partnership with Spain's Banco Central Hispanoamericano.
Traders in Bogota and Medellin said the bank's shares plummeted by about 10 percent to 361 pesos per share before trading was suspended for a 30-minute "cooling off period."

The stock cut its losses soon after trading resumed, however, and ended down just 1.25 percent at 395 pesos per share. "Banco de Colombia registered the most dramatic movement any stock has shown in a single session this year," one Bogota-based dealer said of the see-saw trading. Although the bank's shares pared their losses considerably, he noted that they remained below book value. "It's the cheapest stock on the market," he said.

The day's big winner was Cementos Argos of the Sindicato Antioqueno conglomerate. Brokers in Medellin, where 639 million pesos of Argos stock changed hands, said it closed up 3.63 percent at 8,500 pesos per share on demand by local investors and cross-trades by existing stockholders.
Banco de Bogota was also among gainers but it added just 0.16 percent in the capital, closing at 6,511 pesos per share.
"Good financial results are expected from Bogota in the first quarter and that's where the demand originated," a broker said.
